inventory.method: re-classification of reproit-lab/defect-candidates-winui.json, which was grouped by repository, plus a GitHub GraphQL scan of merged pull requests that close at least one issue
inventory.candidateDefectsMeaning: merged pull requests closing an issue; for UniGetUI the count is restricted to pull requests merged before the Avalonia-only cutover so that it covers WinUI 3 revisions only
inventory.frameworkVerification: git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout, then git show <revision>:<project file> at every revision named in this record; a repository is never classified by its default branch
inventory.note: the 127-entry winui candidate inventory does not survive re-classification: only two of its nine repositories are WinUI 3 applications at the revisions in question, and one of those two is rejected below. The second qualified application was not found in that inventory at all; it came from a separate GitHub code search for project files containing both UseWinUI and WindowsPackageType, which returned 2732 hits across 605 distinct repositories, ranked by whether the repository is an end-user application with an issue tracker that links its fixes

applicationPool.reason: src/UniGetUI/UniGetUI.csproj sets UseWinUI>true with WindowsPackageType None and WindowsAppSDKSelfContained true on net8.0-windows10.0.26100.0, verified at all ten revisions named below, so it is a real WinUI 3 application that runs unpackaged with no MSIX, no package identity and no signing certificate. Containment: package install, update and uninstall flows drive winget, scoop, chocolatey and npm and mutate machine state, so only settings, navigation, keyboard and package-list triggers are in bounds and the package managers must be left uninitialised or stubbed. The repository moved from marticliment/UniGetUI to Devolutions/UniGetUI

the second independent application. src/DLSS Swapper.csproj sets UseWinUI>true with WindowsPackageType None and WindowsAppSDKSelfContained true on net9.0-windows10.0.26100.0 and later net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0, and the repository contains zero Package.appxmanifest files at every revision named below, so there is no MSIX, no package identity and no signing certificate anywhere in the build. It is a real end-user desktop application, not a sample or a library. Containment: the product's headline action replaces DLSS, FSR and XeSS DLLs inside game install directories and can write NVIDIA driver profiles through NvAPI, which is state outside its own profile, so only settings, navigation, language, window-state and search triggers are in bounds and the run must start with an empty game library. Its own state lives under the user profile and it refuses to run elevated for import and export, so the in-bounds triggers touch nothing outside the profile. Build caveat: nuget.config adds the anonymous CommunityToolkit Labs feed on pkgs.dev.azure.com alongside nuget.org, needed for CommunityToolkit.Labs.WinUI.Controls.MarkdownTextBlock; both are public and unauthenticated but nuget.org alone is not sufficient
applicationPool.candidateDefectsBasis: 81 of the 190 merged pull requests cite a real issue number in their Issues Resolved section, 31 of those are marked as a bug fix, and GitHub auto-links four closed issues to a merged pull request. The offline, no-game, no-swap subset is far smaller; three pairs are verified below

selectedDefects.issueTitle: [BUG] UniGetUI reacts to key press although not focused
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Use KeyDown instead of KeyUp to handle MainView keyboard shortcuts

frameworkVerified.evidence: UseWinUI>true, WindowsPackageType None, WindowsAppSDKSelfContained true, TargetFramework net8.0-windows10.0.26100.0

build.toolchain: .NET 8 SDK with the 10.0.26100 Windows SDK reference pack

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the shortcut handler is bound to KeyUp on the WinUI page, so a key released over the window is handled even when the key was pressed while the window did not have focus. The adapter exercises it exactly through its two primitives: set focus with the UI Automation focus pattern, deliver a key sequence, then read back which page the navigation tree reports as selected. It is a WinUI 3 XAML routed-event defect, meaningless outside a XAML input pipeline, so it is proper evidence for this adapter rather than for .NET generally
remaining: prove the application starts with all package managers disabled so that no winget or scoop process is spawned during the run
define how the harness moves focus away from the window and back without leaving the target's own automation tree
build both revisions in the native x86_64 Windows VM and record the exact SDK versions

selectedDefects.issueTitle: [BUG] Crash in v1.2 when trying to get to settings

frameworkVerified.evidence: UseWinUI>true, WindowsPackageType None, WindowsAppSDKSelfContained true, TargetFramework net9.0-windows10.0.26100.0, PackageReference Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK 1.7.250606001; the tree contains no Package.appxmanifest at either revision

build.toolchain: .NET 9 SDK with the 10.0.26100 Windows SDK reference pack

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the affected revision calls DriverSettingsSession.CreateAndLoad through NvAPIWrapper without first checking that nvapi64.dll can be loaded, so on a machine with no NVIDIA driver the process dies while opening the settings or game page. The fix probes the library with LoadLibrary and degrades instead. The native x86_64 Windows VM has no NVIDIA GPU, so the reproduction condition is the environment we already have rather than something the harness must fabricate, exactly as the react-native-ios offline-import candidate is defined by its offline path. The adapter drives it with one navigation action and one observation: click the settings item in the UI Automation navigation tree, then ask whether the window and its automation tree still exist. It is the cheapest possible liveness oracle and it needs no game library, no network and no swap
remaining: confirm the crash is a process exit rather than a caught exception, so the observable is a definite absent automation tree and not a timeout

selectedDefects.issueTitle: DLSS Swapper opens but doesn't let me access it
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Fixes an issue where closing a window while minimized won't yeet it to -32000 x/y pos

frameworkVerified.evidence: UseWinUI>true, WindowsPackageType None, WindowsAppSDKSelfContained true, TargetFramework net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0, PackageReference Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK 1.8.260101001; the tree contains no Package.appxmanifest at either revision

build.toolchain: .NET 10 SDK with the 10.0.26100 Windows SDK reference pack

selectedDefects.whySuitable: Windows parks a minimized window at x and y of -32000, and on the affected revision the persistence code stores that position on exit and restores it on the next launch, so the application starts permanently offscreen. The trigger is minimize, close, relaunch; the observable is the BoundingRectangle the window element reports to UI Automation, which is the most adapter-native geometric assertion available on Windows and cannot be read at all without a live automation tree. It is entirely offline, needs no game library and writes only the application's own settings file
remaining: prove the harness can minimize and restore the window through the UI Automation window pattern rather than through a raw Win32 call, otherwise the trigger leaves the target's own automation tree
